In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the improved fallow was the most risk efficient cropping system, followed by continuous rice, and then the natural bush fallows.

the improved fallow cropping system dominated the other two systems, based on grain yield and average income risk-efficiency criteria, and that the natural bush fallows cropping system was dominated by the improved cover crop system, under both fertilizer regimes.
the cover crop fallow treatment was the most efficient in terms of risk and return, followed by the bush fallow, with the continuous rice treatment least efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the improved cover crop system dominated the natural bush-fallow system, based on yield, average farm income, and income risk-efficiencies.
the use of a cover crop in a fallow system is superior to the use of natural vegetation in the fallow system.
the leguminous fallow system was the most risk efficient system, followed by continuous rice and then the natural bush fallows.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of leguminous cover crops can improve the productivity and risk efficiency of rice production in the Guinean Savannah of Ghana.
the use of cover crops in rice production can be an effective way to reduce risk and increase income for farmers in northern Ghana.
farmers can increase their income and risk efficiency by adopting improved fallow systems.
